name: Contains Duplicate II
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return true if there are two distinct indices i and j in the array such that nums[i] == nums[j] and abs(i - j) <= k.
shortDescription: Check if duplicate exists within k distance

methods.name: computeWithHashMap
methods.label: Hash map

methods.name: computeWithHashSet
methods.label: Hash set

methods.name: computeWithBruteForce
methods.label: Brute force

explanation.idea: You only care about repeats that are close: within k positions. Remember where each value was last seen, or keep just the last k values in view.
explanation.analogy: A bouncer who only remembers the last k faces: if someone in that recent memory walks in again, they came back too soon.

computeWithHashMap.summary: Store each value's latest index; a repeat within k is a hit.
steps: For each index i, look up the last index of nums[i].
If it exists and i − last ≤ k, return true.
Update the map to the newest index i.

computeWithHashSet.summary: Keep a set of the last k values; slide it forward.
steps: If nums[i] is already in the window set, return true.
When the set has more than k values, remove nums[i − k], the one that just fell out of range.
computeWithHashSet.timeWhy: One pass with O(1) set operations.
computeWithHashSet.spaceWhy: The window never holds more than k + 1 values.

computeWithBruteForce.summary: For each i, compare with the next k elements.
steps: For each i, check j from i + 1 to i + k.
Any equal pair is a hit.
computeWithBruteForce.timeWhy: Up to k comparisons per element.

pitfalls: Keeping the first index instead of the latest in the map misses closer repeats.
Off-by-one: the distance allowed is ≤ k, so the window holds k elements behind the current one.
interview: This is the classic introduction to a fixed-size sliding window: say "I only need the last k values".
Follow-up (Contains Duplicate III): values within t of each other → a TreeSet window with floor/ceiling, or buckets.
